I see you are still failing the tests, which is down to a port publishing issue AFAIK. Some clients have issues handling both Discv4 and Discv5 on the same UDP port (<@&836981603216654336>, maybe also <@&1070471163219824730> ?). The issue with this is that you would have to switch version at one point, and that will break communications between your own versions. In Geth we have a simple fall-through design: get packet, if it's not v4, pass it on to next handler, which happens to be v5. You can find the gist of it here for reference: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/918d46b942b9d9f2a13c02cf12a651ba9ccae879/p2p/discover/v4_udp.go#L555-L563 <@741651225576996935>, please check above https://github.com/ethereum/hive/pull/1501 pls for reth yeah i think this is fine for reth. reth already has shared-port support, so setting `--discovery.v5.port=30303` doesn’t make it bind two separate sockets. it triggers the shared socket path: discv5 owns the socket and anything it doesn’t recognize gets forwarded into discv4, basically the same fall-through idea as geth but the other way around. the hive failure was just testing discv5 on `30303` while reth was listening on `9200`. merged <@761154847432769577> could you check? Besu either run with disvc4 or discv5. I'll check the latest hive tests failure and report back.

Some clients have issues handling both Discv4 and Discv5 on the same UDP port (<@&836981603216654336>, maybe also <@&1070471163219824730> ?). The issue with this is that you would have to switch version at one point, and that will break communications between your own versions.

You can find the gist of it here for reference: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/918d46b942b9d9f2a13c02cf12a651ba9ccae879/p2p/discover/v4_udp.go#L555-L563

excerpts.author: emmajamiesonhoare_30642
excerpts.content:
yeah i think this is fine for reth. reth already has shared-port support, so setting `--discovery.v5.port=30303` doesn’t make it bind two separate sockets.

it triggers the shared socket path: discv5 owns the socket and anything it doesn’t recognize gets forwarded into discv4, basically the same fall-through idea as geth but the other way around.

the hive failure was just testing discv5 on `30303` while reth was listening on `9200`.
